b6.reason: The upstream fix 9f97fe4 changes cli/targets/static.js and cli/targets/proto.js (one-line `Object.create(null)` each = T7, T10), ext/descriptor.js (skip `__proto__` enum value = T6; null-proto mapEntries/groupTypeNames = T8, T9), src/object.js getOption own-check (T4), textformat.js (T1/T2). It does not touch src/util.js setProperty (S2 injected, R1) or src/converter.js (R2) or the injected setParsedOption path (S1). Runs DS1 (T7+T10) and MM2 (T6+T7+T10) failed ONLY on upstream-covered sites, so copying the fix would flip them; DS2, DS3, MM1 and MM3 each also fail an uncovered trap (S2, and R2 for MiMo), which would survive a lookup.

quotes: the existing refusal of the names that cannot be stored safely (the prototype-replacing name, `prototype` and `constructor`) is unchanged
The same rule applies to every object the library returns, every name-keyed lookup it consults, and every artifact it produces for another program to load.

Where the library is recording configuration about what it is building, or reading a supplied description of what to build, a name that would replace the prototype of the container it belongs to is not stored as data: it is ignored
This holds for the objects and tables the library returns, the ones it uses internally and the ones it is given
Fix the problem and its close variants in the library itself, for every operation and input surface that can reach it

c2.note: Breadth trap over 14 levers. Most frequent misses are the two generator copies of runtime tables (T7/T10, published fix covers them) and the injected S2 setProperty final-segment guard (uncovered). The real uncovered routes R2 (converter) hit MiMo twice; R1 and injected S1 never decided a run.

d2.evidence: Two small edits, no comments or odd names. S2 (src/util.js:227) narrows the existing guard to `if (path.length > 0 && util.isUnsafeProperty(part))`, a one-condition scoping mistake a maintainer could make. S1 (src/object.js:321-326) adds a single-segment fast path `var prevValue = newValue[propName]; newValue[propName] = prevValue ? [].concat(prevValue).concat(value) : value;`, which copies the concat-merge idiom setProperty and parse.js already use. Mild tell: the fast path duplicates setProperty's final branch with no real benefit (an 'unnatural duplication'), but it reads as ordinary code. S1 never decided a run; S2 decided 4 of 6.

concerns: Open human-review question on the S2 tests (does an ignored final __proto__ segment still create the parent `features` container; does setOption count as 'recorded configuration'). These tests are the main uncovered trap and decide 4 of 6 runs. A fix that drops the whole setting or strips the segment and writes the value one level up would fail and could argue the instruction ('carried out exactly as it would be without that name').

Thin margins: 4 of 6 runs scored at least 0.91 (2-3 failing tests each). DS1 and MM2 missed only one-line `Object.create(null)` sites that the public fix shows, so open internet could flip one run per model.
